subject: Meteorology
title: Aristotle's Meteorologica
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Aristotle's Meteorologica.

hook.text: In 340 BCE, Aristotle wrote Meteorologica—the first systematic attempt to explain weather, clouds, and wind.

buildup.text: He proposed that two exhalations from Earth—moist and dry—caused rain, wind, thunder, and earthquakes.

discovery.text: Meteorologica gave the field its name—'meteora' meant things in the sky, covering everything above ground level.

twist.text: Many of Aristotle's explanations were wrong—but his framework of natural causes replaced mythology with observation.

climax.text: His work dominated Western weather thinking for nearly 2,000 years—until instruments proved him wrong.

punchline.text: Wrong about the answers—but right about asking the questions.

quiz.question: What does the word 'meteorology' derive from?
options: Greek 'meteora' meaning things in the sky
